top_choice_rationale: Optical lattice clocks are a mature, experimentally demonstrated measurement advance: magic-wavelength trapping of many neutral atoms took frequency uncertainty to the 10^-18 level, has been reproduced by several independent groups, and has opened new work in metrology, geodesy and tests of fundamental physics. The Katori and Ye allocation is clean with a narrow, defensible citation. P002 is a real discovery with an experimental confirmation, but its allocation is contested (Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the 3D work) and the first observation rests largely on one group, so I rank it second, still ahead of no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; Katori and Ye are in precision laser spectroscopy, a neighbouring field, and Kroll's PhD stay in John Hall's lab (Ye's mentor) is at most a distant link
